newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia foils planned rebel attacks in capital.
newsitem.headline: Colombia foils planned rebel attacks in capital.

text.p: Colombian rebels have drawn up plans to attack the presidential palace and other high-profile targets in Bogota in a bid to move their war from the countryside to the streets of the capital, authorities said on Friday.

Defence Minister Juan Carlos Esguerra said the rebel's plans to unleash concentrated attacks in the capital were uncovered by police and military intelligence officials in a clandestine operation that ended at dawn on Friday with the seizure of a guerrilla arsenal on the outskirts of Bogota.

The arsenal, complete with a map pinpointing strategic targets around Bogota, included 18 armour-piercing rockets, 75 rifle-launched grenades, mortar rounds and vast quantities of ammunition, authorities said.
"We're happy to have avoided what really might have been a catastrophe," said National Police chief Gen. Rosso Jose Serrano, who spoke alongside Esguerra at a news conference.

Serrano said the "terrorist action in Bogota," masterminded by leaders of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), was to have included attacks on the Defence Ministry and National Police headquarters as well as the ornate Casa de Narino presidential palace in the city centre.
The FARC also had selected six police barracks and an unspecified number of diplomatic missions for attack, Serrano said.

Police conducted summary searches of 48 suspected FARC safehouses, and arrested nine rebels in Bogota and the northern cities of Bucaramanga and Cucuta, before uncovering the extent of the rebel plot to lay siege to the capital, police sources said.
The FARC, founded as a Marxist, pro-Soviet group in 1964, is Colombia's largest and oldest guerrilla group.

Military officials say it has deteriorated in recent years into little more than a rag-tag band of drug traffickers, bandits and kidnappers. But diplomats say it demonstrated that it is a force to be reckoned by launching a nationwide offensive in late August that caught the military totally off guard.

Scores of police and soliders were killed in the offensive and at least 60 soldiers are still being held prisoner after FARC rebels overran their military base in jungle-covered southern Putumayo province.
